Note::TexAccessor::captions¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::captions() const

Extract Displayed Caption Bodies Per Source Cell¶

captions() extracts the required brace body from each complete \caption or \caption* command. It is useful when figure and table descriptions must be indexed or analyzed independently of the surrounding environment.

An optional square-bracket argument is accepted but not returned: in \caption[Short]{Displayed title}, the token is Displayed title. This reflects the distinction between the abbreviated list entry and the caption body presented with the object. Starred commands are recognized in the same source order as unstarred commands, and repeated captions remain repeated.

The extractor is deliberately lexical. The required body must be a complete, non-nested brace group. A body containing another brace group, such as \caption{A \textbf{bold} title}, is not partially returned. Run a suitable normalization first when nested formatting must be flattened, or use a parser when arbitrary TeX nesting must be understood. Comments are ordinary source to this method; call strip_comments() first if commented-out commands must be excluded.

The closed TokenBatch stores all caption bodies in its rank-1 Text tokens() Note. Its Int64 offsets() has source.numel() + 1 entries, so flattened source cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). The original rank and shape determine lane order but are not imposed on a ragged token count. The receiver is not mutated.

Undefined yields undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Empty cells, malformed commands, and cells without captions produce empty intervals. Only Text is accepted. Extraction scans source bytes and allocates the captured bodies and one offset per source cell.

Example 1: Long, Starred, Optional, Missing, And Nested Captions¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(\caption{Long title} \caption*[Short]{Starred long})",
        "no caption", R"(\caption[TOC title]{Displayed title})",
        R"(\caption{Nested \textbf{title}})"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto captions = source.tex().captions();

std::cout << captions.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Long title", "Starred long", "Displayed title"]

The optional Short and TOC title values are not caption bodies. The nested fourth command is ignored rather than truncated.

Example 2: Matrix Cells Retain Ragged Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = captions.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 3, 3]

Flattened matrix cell 0 owns two captions, cell 1 none, cell 2 one, and cell 3 none.

Example 3: Native Integer Cells Reject¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().captions();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "captions Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

captions Int64: rejected
